sentences.text: Fylax is a genus of hadrosauroid ornithopod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Spain, known only from a nearly complete left dentary bone.
The name Fylax thyrakolasus means 'keeper of the gates of hell,' referencing the dinosaur's proximity to the Cretaceous-Paleogene mass extinction event.

The holotype specimen, designated IPS-36338, was discovered in the early 1990s in the Figuerola Formation in Lleida province, northeastern Spain, and was initially described as a distinct fossil in 1999.
Fylax lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 68 to 66 million years ago, specifically within the Maastrichtian stage from approximately 72.2 to 66 million years ago, in what is now Europe.

Later phylogenetic analyses in 2026 failed to recover the close relationship between Fylax and Tethyshadros that was initially proposed in 2021. Using updated matrices, some researchers placed Fylax as an early-diverging member of the Hadrosauridae rather than as a non-hadrosaurid hadrosauromorph.
